_comment: THE LAST CUSTOMER (GDD 26). Written 2026-08-12, reworked 2026-08-13 (the author): the beat is a TRIAL now -- an inspector's visit in the shape of a service. The guest is a GUEST OF THE HOUSE: no licence (they say who they are), no bill, no rating -- the run's books never see them. They arrive into a conversation; when the talking ends the clock starts, and they ask for a RUN of drinks against that one clock, ONE AT A TIME (the post-it shows the drink in hand, never the list). The standard: exactly the drink, made the way the book says, garnished as asked; fill is the one forgiveness at >= 0.90 of the glass. Wrong drink = a mistake, the ask stays; past allowedMistakes or past the clock, the night is failed and the beat returns on ITS OWN NIGHT, returnsAfterWeeks later. GUESTS COME AT THE WEEKEND (friday/saturday, refused otherwise); only the host may work a quiet night, which is why Ece's beat zero is the opening Tuesday. Because asks are revealed one at a time, the shopping warning lives in needStyle and in the HOST'S lines, days early -- that is what the quiet nights are for. THE BAR OPENED THIS WEEK: nothing here may lean on the room having a past. Every ask is an id in recipes.json, every look a slug in papers.json, every needStyle a style the market sells. Names and lines are the author's to replace; the SHAPE is the design.

characters.blurb: Works the shift with you. Has done this before, in rooms that did not make it. Takes the first last call herself.
Collects for the building. Never raises his voice, never has to.
Four hundred thousand people watch her drink. She never says where she is until she has left.
Inspects rooms like this one. Orders the same drinks everywhere, on purpose, and counts the seconds.

ask: Door is shut. Pour me one of whatever we actually have.
Owner's first night. It is a rule somewhere.
nudge: Anything on that shelf. I am not the difficult one.
servedRight: Not bad for a room that did not exist last week.
The ones who come after me will count your seconds. I do not.
servedWrong: That is not what I asked for, and I am the easy one.
declined: You are turning down the bartender. Bold.

ask: So you are the one who took it on.
A whiskey, neat. Then another. I drink the second one slower.
nudge: Still no bourbon on that shelf.
hostWarning: Friday is the man from the building. Get a bourbon in before then.
He will not ask twice, and he will not ask for anything clever.
servedRight: The building can wait a week. Do not make me come back to check.
servedWrong: That is not whiskey, and we both know it.
declined: Then buy a bottle. I will come back.
hostBefore: That one is here about the building, not the whiskey.
hostAfter: He will be back. They always come back to see if you lasted.

ask: Do not look at the phone, it is not filming. Yet.
A mule, the real kind. Then something clear for the second take.
nudge: No ginger, no mule, no post. That is the whole equation.
hostWarning: Saturday needs ginger in the well. Buy it now, not on the night.
She films the drink, not you. Make it look like the picture.
servedRight: Okay. THAT is going up tonight.
Four hundred thousand people are about to know this room exists.
servedWrong: I cannot post this. Neither should you.
declined: A room that says no. That is almost content. Almost.
hostBefore: She is why Saturday needs ginger in the well. Trust me on this one.
hostAfter: That is how a room gets found. One post somebody believes.

ask: Three drinks. I will name them one at a time, and I will be counting.
A Manhattan first. Stirred -- I will know the difference.
nudge: Vermouth. It is not an optional ingredient, it is half the drink.
hostWarning: There is a vermouth on the market page. We will need it by Friday.
Three drinks, no second chances, and he counts the seconds. Practise.
servedRight: Stirred, cold, on time. All three.
I inspect rooms like this for a living. This one passes.
servedWrong: You shook it. I can see the ice in it from here.
declined: An honest no is worth a line in the report. Later, then.
hostBefore: I know that face. He wrote the room I worked in out of business. Stir, do not shake.
hostAfter: A pass from him is worth more than a good month. Frame it.

say: Six bottles and a keg. That is a bar, technically.
Read them before you pour — the licence says what they came for.
Click the stool, not the drink.
Nobody tells you what they want until you ask.
Two spirits in one tin do not become a drink on their own.
Shake it or stir it. The book says which.
Beer is not a cocktail. Lean the glass, then straighten it.
The head is the whole job.
Whatever we did not stock tonight, somebody will ask for tomorrow.
Buy narrow. A wide shelf on a new bar is just money standing still.
We do not have what the weekend wants. Yet.
The market opens when the door shuts. Go and fix the shelf.
The till is under the rent. It happens to every room once.
Twice is a habit. Three times is a different bar with your name on it.
